summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including morbid obesity, chronic lymphedema, obstructive sleep apnea, epilepsy, and recurrent cellulitis was admitted for worsening left lower extremity swelling and erythema. She had recently completed a course of antibiotics but symptoms recurred, prompting admission. IV clindamycin and aztreonam were started, then switched to IV vancomycin after consultation with Infectious Disease, given partial response and concern for resistant organisms. The infection improved over five days, and she was transitioned back to oral doxycycline. During the stay, she experienced a brief absence-type seizure with left upper extremity tremors, evaluated by Neurology, who recommended continuing her current antiepileptic regimen with outpatient follow-up. Her chronic pain was managed with oxycodone and morphine, and diuretics were optimized for lymphedema. She was discharged home with services, on her baseline medications including warfarin, with plans for home IV diuretic therapy, neurology follow-up, and avoidance of topical steroids on the legs.
problems: Epilepsy, unspecified, not intractable, without status epilepticus
Morbid (severe) obesity due to excess calories
Personal history of other venous thrombosis and embolism
Personal history of malignant neoplasm of other female genital organs
